flashcard_questions.a: A very large molecule made by joining many monomers in a repeating pattern.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a monomer in polymerisation?
flashcard_questions.a: A small reactive molecule that joins with others to form a polymer chain.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of monomer takes part in addition polymerisation?
flashcard_questions.a: Unsaturated alkenes with a carbon-carbon double bond.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the only product of addition polymerisation?
What happens to the C=C double bond during addition polymerisation?
flashcard_questions.a: It opens up and becomes a single bond in the chain.

flashcard_questions.q: What small molecule is released during condensation polymerisation?
How many functional groups does each condensation monomer carry?
Which link forms when a dicarboxylic acid reacts with a diol?
Which link forms when a dicarboxylic acid reacts with a diamine?
Which two functional groups does every amino acid contain?
flashcard_questions.a: An amine group and a carboxylic acid group.

flashcard_questions.q: What bond forms when two amino acids join together?
flashcard_questions.a: A peptide bond, which is a type of amide link.

flashcard_questions.q: Which natural polymer is built from amino acid monomers?
Which monomer joins repeatedly to make starch?
Which monomer joins repeatedly to make DNA?
Which type of polymerisation forms proteins, starch and DNA?

notes: 15 cards: 5 term to definition, 4 monomer-to-polymer pairings, 2 link-formation cards (ester and amide, kept distinct to avoid interference), 4 what-happens-if. Dropped the poly(ethene) monomer card because the answer sits inside the polymer name in the question, and dropped the n-subscript drawing convention and PVC naming to stay inside 15.
